card.name: Words after 'not' in safety limits
card.fires_on: The word right after a negation such as 'have not' or 'has not', or inside 'safety of', in statements that something is unestablished or not studied. Also seen in 'discount not applicable'.

modes.label: Not established
modes.description: The word 'been' after 'have not' or 'has not' in statements that safety or effectiveness is not established.
modes.example: The safety and effectiveness of ALVESCO have not<< been>> established in pediatric patients less than 1

modes.label: Safety of unstudied use
modes.description: The word 'of' or 'in' after 'safety' when the text goes on to describe an untested dose or population.
modes.example: The safety<< of>> using more than 18 doses in

modes.label: Not applicable offer
modes.description: The word 'not' or 'applicable' in a web discount disclaimer.
modes.example: *Discount<< not>> applicable on SES Online products.

card.writes: It pushes toward limiting words like 'cannot' and 'only', which fit statements of restriction.
card.plain: It marks spots in a sentence where the text is saying something has not been shown or is not allowed.
